items.evidence: REPRODUCES (both parts). Vanilla 26.1 still has the OLD selector parser — the option-state refactor (InvertableSetOptionState, SetOnceOptionState) that closed this defect for 26.2 had NOT happened yet in 26.1 (neither class exists in 26.1's EntitySelectorOptions/EntitySelectorParser); the Rust parser (selector.rs) implements the 26.2 option-state shape. (a) Duplicate options: vanilla 26.1's EntitySelectorOptions.get() runs the canUse gate BEFORE the value is read but does NOT roll back (only the unknown-option branch does setCursor(start)); the inapplicable branch throws at the cursor as it stands, i.e. at the END of the option name. Rust rolls back to the option-name START (selector.rs:333-341). For @e[type=pig,type=cow] the cursors differ by the option-name length (4 for type). (b) @a[type=player]: vanilla 26.1's type canUse is !parser.isTypeLimited() (lambda$bootStrap$42), and @a/@p/@r call limitToType(EntityType.PLAYER) during parseSelector, so vanilla 26.1 REJECTS it; Rust pushes minecraft:player into s.types without marking type_option (selector.rs:218-242), so can_use("type") stays true and Rust ACCEPTS it. (The run that would flag both parts empirically is blocked - B9-H01; the verdict rests on the javap + source.)
items.title: Selector option errors (1.21.7) — reproduces: vanilla 26.1 predates the selector refactor the Rust parser implements
